answer: Storage is bound to identity by a replication proof that is hard to satisfy with shared bytes, and because the sealed data is unique per identity, aliases and thin-provisioned clones fail the proof at their next challenge. Each head pays its own cost, paid in full, since the cost is per identity. Every account owns a terrace, answers a karst, and is named by a pulse: a farm can mint pulse bindings instantly, but the terrace behind each one is disk, and the karst will catch the ones that share it. The attacker therefore pays for real storage per head.
